newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian 1996 coal output seen up by 4.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian 1996 coal output seen up by 4.6 pct.

text.p: Bulgaria expects its 1996 coal output to rise to 32.16 million tonnes from last year's 30.76 million tonnes, energy officials said on Monday.
Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources and heavily relies on its nuclear plant at Kozloduy, plans to generate more electricity from local coal this winter, energy officials said.

But Bulgaria, which produces mainly lignite coal, will import 1.5 million tonnes of Ukranian coal, 700,000 tonnes of Vietnamese coal and some 500,000 tonnes of Russian coal as coal-fired plants meet half of the country's energy needs.
The imported high quality coal will be mainly for the 1,260-megawatt Varna coal and gas-fired power plant, which has been idle since 1995 due to a lack of cash for coal imports.
A government report said the Varna plant had some 350,000 tonnes of imported coal on storage now and more regular supplies were expected this winter.
Another 330,000 tonnes of local and imported coal are stored at a thermal plant in Bobovdol, with a capacity of 600 megawatts, the report added.

The European Union has granted 10 million Ecus to Bulgaria's energy sector as compensation for the closure of a controversial Kozloduy reactor for safety tests. Half of the grant was aimed at purchasing high quality coal.
In August the Bulgarian government lined up technical procedures for closing down four inefficient underground coal mines.
